bug_semantics: On Linux/Unix, LocalFolderExtractor first constructs and canonicalizes new File(destination, archiveEntryName) while backslashes in the untrusted RAR name are still literal filename characters. A name such as '..\..\tmp\evil' therefore passes the destination-prefix check. If the file does not exist, makeFile then splits that same name on backslashes and rejoins the components with File.separator, turning the previously literal '..' components into real '/' traversal. extract subsequently opens FileOutputStream on that reconstructed path and writes attacker-controlled archive content outside the extraction directory.
flaw_origin: The causal flaw is the two-stage, inconsistent interpretation of an archive pathname: validation and use do not operate on the same normalized representation. The backslash-splitting/reconstruction and write path first appear in the repository's root initial-import commit 6f32323c983015d96c64084418793853f514b519 in testutil/src/main/java/de/innosystec/unrar/testutil/ExtractArchive.java. That implementation was later promoted and moved through production paths without changing the mechanism; e60b915f8932c08b9b6874a97f00676decba069a added canonical-path validation but left it before the separator reinterpretation, creating the advisory's explicit validation bypass rather than originating the underlying arbitrary-write mechanism.
ai_marker: absent — `git cat-file -p 6f32323c983015d96c64084418793853f514b519` shows author and committer `Edmund Wagner <edmund-wagner@web.de>` at Unix time 1284206829 (+0200), message `initial import`, no bot identity, no Co-Authored-By trailer, no Generated-with trailer, and no other AI marker in the BIC commit object.
evidence: The first-party advisory GHSA-j273-m5qq-6825 / CVE-2026-28208 identifies LocalFolderExtractor.createFile/makeFile, affected Maven versions < 7.5.8, first patched version 7.5.8, and direct fix https://github.com/junrar/junrar/commit/947ff1d33f00f940aa68ae2593500291d799d954.

`git show 6f32323c983015d96c64084418793853f514b519:testutil/src/main/java/de/innosystec/unrar/testutil/ExtractArchive.java` shows createFile taking the archive-controlled name, makeFile executing `name.split("\\\\")`, rebuilding `path` with File.separator and `..` components, creating that file, and extractArchive opening FileOutputStream on the returned path. Thus the root commit already contains the path reinterpretation and attacker-content write sink.

`git cat-file -p 6f32323c983015d96c64084418793853f514b519` contains a tree, author, committer, and message but no `parent` header. `git show` presents the vulnerable ExtractArchive.java as a new file from /dev/null, so the vulnerable lines are absent from the immediate predecessor (the empty pre-root tree); introducer_parent is necessarily null because this is the repository root.

History reconstruction distinguishes moves from origin: 7e0c503f3afe6da766e4476333bc3ee9cd677bb1 renamed the package/project; e5b90d174c5a426a134b00a33ddece3ac9e82a39 promoted the extractor from testutil into the unrar module; bb362df3e1e5471e58f6322c91b7b1c9a8ebaef1 moved the module tree; 75cb6a58c9b3ca08db954eec241b91a5331dd632 inlined the same mechanism into Junrar.java; and 3b645d991563dd8933f6efab135cd76a43a92d6b moved it into LocalFolderExtractor.java. These are lineage/promotional moves, not smaller commits that first wrote the flawed logic.

`git show e60b915f8932c08b9b6874a97f00676decba069a -- src/main/java/com/github/junrar/LocalFolderExtractor.java` shows the later canonical-path startsWith guard added before the already-existing makeFile backslash split. This explains why the Linux/Unix exploit is a validation/use mismatch rather than a flaw introduced by that attempted mitigation.

`git show 947ff1d33f00f940aa68ae2593500291d799d954 -- src/main/java/com/github/junrar/LocalFolderExtractor.java` shows the direct repair: normalize `\` to `/` before constructing/canonicalizing the checked File, then split the same normalized name on `/` in makeFile. The check and use therefore consume the same pathname representation.

Version-boundary checks resolve v7.5.7 to 04481cf28bb121b976077b3ab7d7e1adec82687f and v7.5.8 to 97bf405418d0997717d55e0556045ff80945e099. `git merge-base --is-ancestor` confirms the BIC is an ancestor of v7.5.7, the fix is not an ancestor of v7.5.7 (exit 1), and the fix is an ancestor of v7.5.8. Source at v7.5.7 has raw `fh.getFileName()` plus `name.split("\\\\")`; v7.5.8 has `invariantSeparatorsPathString(fh.getFileName())`, `name.split("/")`, and the normalization helper. `git tag --contains 947ff1d33f00f940aa68ae2593500291d799d954` starts at v7.5.8.
BIC-only AI attribution uses the root commit object quoted in ai_marker; no PR text, later commit, fix authorship, or branch metadata was used.
reasoning: The advisory attack path is reachable through Junrar.extract: an untrusted RAR filename is checked in one separator representation, reinterpreted in another by makeFile, and finally used by FileOutputStream. Following the exact splitting/reconstruction lines backward shows repeated renames and moves, not fresh introductions. The first repository commit already wrote the complete flawed extraction path, so 6f32323c983015d96c64084418793853f514b519 is the smallest available real BIC; its lack of a parent directly establishes pre-root absence and justifies a null introducer_parent. The 2019 canonical check was an incomplete mitigation layered over this older mechanism, while 947ff1d33f00f940aa68ae2593500291d799d954 is the direct 2026 fix because it normalizes before validation and preserves that representation during construction. Tag ancestry and tag-source inspection place the vulnerable implementation in v7.5.7 and the direct fix in v7.5.8. Finally, the BIC commit object has ordinary human author/committer identities and no AI-related trailer or bot marker, so under BIC-only attribution the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
